q: what is the Golden Record on Voyager
tell me about the Golden Record on the Voyager spacecrafts
what is on the Golden Record
a: The Voyager Golden Record is a phonograph record included on both Voyager 1 and Voyager 2 spacecraft launched by NASA in 1977. Designed by a committee chaired by Carl Sagan, it is a time capsule intended to communicate the story of Earth to any intelligent extraterrestrial life that might find the spacecraft. The record contains 116 images of Earth and its inhabitants, natural sounds (wind, thunder, birds, whales), musical selections from different cultures and eras (Bach, Beethoven, Mozart, Chuck Berry, Louis Armstrong, Azerbaijani bagpipes, Javanese gamelan, and more), greetings in 55 languages including ancient Akkadian and a whale song, and a printed message from President Jimmy Carter. The record is made of copper plated with gold (to protect it from micrometeorite impacts) and is encased in a protective aluminum cover with engraved instructions for playback, including a diagram of the hydrogen atom (the most common element in the universe) as a time reference and a map showing the location of Earth relative to 14 pulsars. The cover also includes a diagram of the record player stylus and the correct playback speed (16.67 RPM). The Golden Record has been described as a message in a bottle cast into the cosmic ocean. Voyager 1 entered interstellar space in 2012 and is now over 24 billion kilometers from Earth. The records are expected to last for billions of years in the vacuum of space.
